title: Listen in on the Sounds of a Jurassic Period Forest - Nautilus
gist: Paleontologists have reconstructed the calls of katydids from a 165-million-year-old Jurassic forest in Mongolia by examining the file-and-plectrum sound-making structures preserved in fossils.

insights.claim: Paleontologists recreated the melodies of katydids that lived roughly 165 million years ago in a Jurassic forest in Mongolia.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Demonstrates that acoustic behavior of extinct insects can be inferred from fossils, expanding paleo-bioacoustics.
insights.locator: there were katydids, insects in the order Orthoptera

insights.claim: The reconstruction was achieved by examining the katydid's delicate file and plectrum structures preserved in fossils, the anatomy that produces their sound.
insights.speaker: Devin Reese
insights.so_what: Shows the specific morphological method that lets researchers infer sound from fossilized structures.
insights.locator: examining the katydid’s delicate file and plectrum structure via fossils
